title: A working week, in your household’s own rhythm
question: Choose a direction for the phone-first planning and shopping prototype. Each uses the same five task destinations and ordinary web controls.

options.label: The Family Album
options.thesis: A readable dinner sequence links this week’s cooking, leftovers, and shopping without turning the plan into a scorecard.
options.viewport: A slate-blue shell, a seven-day meal list with dates and capacity, and one clear Review shopping action; linked leftover dinners reveal their source inline.
options.risk: Personal meal storytelling can crowd the task; captions and history must stay secondary to plan decisions.
options.lineage: Household album sequencing and caption rhythm

raised.raise: Every save and exception state gets the same precise, visible place in the work area.
The weekly sequence has decisive hierarchy and one focal decision, rather than equal-weight tiles.
Type scale does the organizing: dates, meals, and supporting evidence have unmistakable ranks.

options.label: The Neighborhood Notice
options.thesis: An orderly household week uses direct headings, clear date divisions, and visible shopping readiness.
options.viewport: Five task destinations frame a dense week list, with incomplete ingredients and changed capacity surfaced beside the dinner they affect.
options.risk: The familiar noticeboard hierarchy can become ordinary; the distinctive move must stay in useful weekly readiness.
options.lineage: Community notices and dated household coordination

options.label: The Meal Index
options.thesis: Compact, consistently sized meal entries make a large recipe library and a busy week easy to scan.
options.viewport: The standard app shell contains seven compact dinner entries and a searchable meal index; selection remains a labeled button, with no tiny coded controls.
options.risk: Density helps the recipe library more than a hurried phone user; dinner actions must not shrink to thumbnails.
options.case: Product clarity improves for large libraries; household identification is weaker than the dinner sequence.

options.label: The Weekly Mix
options.thesis: Dinner rows give a week a clear rhythm, with active effort aligned beside each meal and capacity explained in plain words.
options.viewport: The normal Plan screen shows seven dated rows, known hands-on effort, explicit hands-off labels, and a shopping summary; no tape controls or physical flip navigation.
options.risk: The metaphor must remain in rhythm alone; timed tape capacity cannot become invented cooking estimates.
options.case: Household familiarity holds; product clarity is less immediate unless effort and leftovers remain explicit.

options.label: The Clear Next Step
options.thesis: Strong labels and a persistent next action make the move from week planning to shopping hard to lose.
options.viewport: A standard five-destination shell frames the week and its exceptions, with a persistent Review shopping button and a clearly labeled saved state.
options.risk: High-salience yellow can dominate an app used for longer recipe reading; content areas need enough quiet.
options.case: Product clarity is stronger for interruptions; household identification is weaker than the dinner sequence.

options.label: The Reference Manual
options.thesis: Structured information distinguishes week decisions from supporting recipe and household evidence.
options.viewport: The standard app shell separates weekly meals, shopping status, and save states; recipe detail remains a conventional reading view.
options.risk: Manual-like density and multiple strong hues make an everyday dinner task feel heavier.
options.case: It loses household identification and immediate task clarity after keeping standard web navigation.
options.kept: A consistent visible location for save and exception states.

options.label: The Focused Week
options.thesis: A dark restrained shell gives one week decision strong focus while names and states stay fully labeled.
options.viewport: A standard week list puts the selected dinner and shopping action in clear focus; no coded names, hidden legends, or hover-only meaning.
options.risk: Dark sparse composition gives too little immediate week information on a phone.
options.case: It loses household identification and week-scanning clarity, even with every label made explicit.
options.kept: One decisive focal task and disciplined visual hierarchy.

options.label: The Type-Led Week
options.thesis: A strong type hierarchy lets the week, dinner names, and supporting evidence carry the screen.
options.viewport: Conventional task navigation surrounds a crisp seven-day list; meal names lead and ingredient/capacity notes follow at a readable scale.
options.risk: The source’s giant display contrasts spend too much phone space on lettering rather than decisions.
options.case: It loses household identification and meal-task clarity once specimen controls are removed.
options.kept: Unmistakable ranks for dates, meal names, and evidence.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar meal-planning app, executed with complete phone and desktop task flows.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional five-tab app with dated dinner rows, grocery checkboxes, and searchable recipe details.
canonCard.risk: Familiar by design, with less distinctive character.
